content.question_text: If an operation cannot be completed because of an error, what two things should the program be able to do?

core_requirements: Allow the user to save all work and terminate the program

content.question_text: When handling errors in code, what four sorts of problems do you need to consider?
What was the traditional reaction to an error in a method (before exceptions)?

core_requirements: Return an error code, or return null

content.question_text: Why can the traditional approach (error codes / null) be problematic?

core_requirements: Returning codes is not an ideal way of pinpointing the actual problem
Returning null can lead to a NullPointerException

content.question_text: What is the alternative, preferred way for a method to deal with an error?

core_requirements: A method can throw an exception

content.question_text: Why are exceptions considered superior to error codes/null for handling errors?

core_requirements: Exceptions are objects that encapsulate the error information
